78.t: Benny Carter's deceptive smile and thorough rehearsals
78.s: Carter is a gentleman whose smile can be deceiving; he rehearses like Don Redman, drawing everything out of a band.
78.ch: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
78.q: He's very thorough in rehearsal of the band. He's another Don Redman. When he rehearses a group, they are well rehearsed. He gets out of you all you've got. but he knows how to explain what he wants...

78.t: Insert on Benny Carter's marking of arrangements
78.s: Carter marked phrasing and shading in his charts, demonstrated on his horn, and had a satisfied smile when the band played it well.
78.ch: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
78.q: ... in his arrangements, and how he wants them played, how he wants this phrased. And if you don't get the idea of what he's talking about, he'll take his horn and show you. His marks are very thorough, how he wants you to do his correct shading, and there he was a dinger at having the right tempo…

541.t: Lessons from Betty Carter: strength, business sense and boot camp
541.s: Harper admired Carter's tenacity, how she created her own concerts, and her tough band as a boot camp.
541.q: A lot of everything. A lot of music, but partly more life than anything. Because one thing about Betty that I always admired was her strength, and she was tenacious. She was going to find a way to get it done. And we miss that. And I think the music misses that, those kind of people like that.…

333.t: Benny Carter as bandleader and the band's hits
333.s: Carter was a perfectionist; he recalls Pom Pom, singing with the band, and Vaughn Monroe covering their hit.
333.q: Benny. Benny Carter was a perfectionist. And he was someone to be looked up to because he was such a great musician. As a matter of fact he was such a great trumpet player until all the trumpet players that ever worked with him looked up to him. He wasn’t that strict you know what I mean? I’m 83,…

336.s: He played with Carter at Yoshi's and Bimbo's; Carter's class and mastery.
336.q: I played with him on two occasions. I played a weekend with him at Yoshi’s — or maybe more. Mel Martin, the saxophone player from the area, put together some stuff for Benny and there was — one was a big band gig right around the corner here at a place called Bimbo’s. And he put together a big band…

104.t: Benny Carter and Gerry Mulligan playing piano on the show
104.s: Both left their horns behind; she calls Carter's style arranger's piano and says Mulligan is a good pianist.
104.q: Well I don’t know why that was. If I wanted him to play his horn — I can’t remember whether he said he forgot it or left it on the table — I think he wanted to play the piano. At least I got that feeling. But I mean he does play sort of nice arranger’s piano but this is a different side of him and…

108.s: He records A Gentleman and His Music, an old idol, and praises Carter's writing.
108.ch: Style, the future of jazz and later playing
108.q: That was nice. Benny Carter is one of the premier musicians of the world. I remember, when I was a kid, my father used to point at him. He said, “Listen. You want to be a musician. You want to listen to people like Benny Carter and Charlie Shavers.” He was an admirer of all these people. He knew…

225.s: Johnson calls Carter a role model as musician, bandleader and man.
225.q: Benny Carter was a role model for me as a musician, as a bandleader, and as a human being and as a man. All of the above.

0.t: Benny Carter's dignified manner and the nickname King
0.s: Carter was always straightforward and dignified; Dickie Wells called him King because he played so much alto.
0.ch: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
0.q: Yeah, Roy was straightforward, straight, you know, and very dignified. We used to -- we're very good friends, kid a lot. I'd say -- we used to call him -- call him King. I mean Dickie Wells started to call him King. 'Hey, King, what you going to play tonight?' Cut out that. 'Hey, King, come on, we…

70.t: Benny Carter and Don Redman as multi-instrumentalists
70.s: Carter plays trombone, trumpet and piano beautifully and can pick up the alto after months and play perfectly; Redman also played several instruments.
70.ch: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
70.q: I know, I know, and a beautiful sound on trumpet. Trumpet players in California, they say, don't like him today because he don't practice and he come on a record date and pick up the horn, and they had been practicing all day, and Bennie would pick up the horn and play it like he played it…

387.t: Benny Carter's band and Doc Cheatham
387.s: Carter's discipline, Teddy Wilson in the band, Dicky Wells and Doc Cheatham's no-pressure playing.
387.q: It was, and in fact Teddy was playing piano before he went with Benny there. Cozy Cole--who were the others? The trombone player.
